summary: Add an explicit shared reactor for independent native collection sources

replay.detail: No history replay or automatic source installation. Source owners capture bounded native facts and explicitly manage namespace installation.

schema.detail: Default Store schema is unchanged. The explicit constructor reuses existing opt-in Views and Installer schema plus schemas supplied by registered source owners.

rules.detail: Admission, canonical ordering, checkpoint rules and digests are unchanged.

compatibility.detail: New crate-internal source lifecycle and scheduler API, including named cache-only sources with no views/operators, borrowed Store access for bounded capture/cut checks, and owned cache actions after successful managed commit and writer return. Explicitly registered Stores attach their shared publisher before exposure; consumer getters only clone prepared state. Source owners certify immutable publications and current lifetime/authority guards even on silent pages. No production source is registered or selected by this change. Sources may explicitly opt into the one shared Publisher with fixed expected identities; named wakes remain distinct graph-watch recheck hints. AfterCommit sources emit a post-swap wake with the original committed token, and the shared reactor emits guarded failure invalidation after writer return. No production native descriptor or retained-root read primitive is supplied.

downtime.detail: No new default startup work or daemon lifecycle change.

manual.detail: No operator action is required; source registration is an explicit application API.

recovery.detail: Logical source callback failures roll back their page or hook bookkeeping and fence only that source and its views. Post-commit action failures cannot undo committed pages; they refuse reads and fence the source. Ordinary commits never repair a fenced source. Precommit SQLite storage failures propagate and roll back, with background writer contention retried. Default Store recovery is unchanged. Consecutive stale publications wait 25 ms through at most 2 s per source, reset on progress or explicit retry, and expose a cumulative stale counter; other sources continue independently. Source open callbacks preserve incompatible persisted identities as unavailable without silently rebinding them or rejecting an otherwise usable Store; each source owns independent identity checks.
